entries.summary: Describe this reusable template with a stable declared name.
details: The name is metadata. A flowgroup’s use_template reference comes from the template file path, which can differ from this value.

entries.summary: Record changes to this reusable definition.
details: Use a string version tag such as "1.0". The runtime does not select a template by version; it loads the referenced file.

entries.summary: Explain when someone should choose this template.
details: Describe the ingestion/transformation pattern and its expected inputs, so users can compare templates before instantiating one.

entries.summary: Apply action defaults when this template expands.
details: List existing action configuration presets. These settings participate in resolution alongside flowgroup presets and explicit action fields.

entries.summary: Declare the inputs supplied when this template is used.
details: Each parameter has a name and can declare required, default and descriptive metadata. Reference it with {{ name }} in action string values.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml:
parameters:
  - name: table_name
    required: true
    description: Name of the source table

entries.summary: Name the value a flowgroup will supply.
details: Use this exact name in {{ parameter_name }} expressions and as a key under template_parameters. Rename deliberately because existing invocations may still use the old name.

entries.summary: Explain the expected value and how the template uses it.
details: Give the input’s purpose, useful examples and any convention a caller must follow. This description guides users but does not add runtime validation.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml: description: Source table name without a catalog or schema

entries.summary: Require each flowgroup to supply this parameter explicitly.
details: Required checks happen before defaults are applied. A default does not satisfy a required parameter; the invocation must include its key.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml:
parameters:
  - name: table_name
    required: true
    default: orders

entries.unsetBehavior: When required is absent, the parameter is optional.

entries.summary: Supply the value used when an optional parameter is omitted.
details: No default differs from an explicit null, false, zero, empty string or collection. A required parameter still needs an explicit invocation entry even if a default is declared.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml:
parameters:
  - name: columns
    required: false
    default: []

entries.summary: Document the intended value type for this parameter.
details: This is advisory metadata. The template engine does not enforce it; rendered-string conversion is heuristic and can change numeric-looking values.

entries.summary: Build the action patterns expanded by this template.
details: Use {{ parameter }} inside supported action string values. The engine renders those values, not mapping keys or arbitrary whole-document Jinja control flow. Preview with representative inputs.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml:
actions:
  - name: "load_{{ table_name }}"
    type: load
    source:
      type: delta
      table: "{{ table_name }}"
    target: "v_{{ table_name }}"
